slides.title: Spoken Tutorial on Understanding APIs
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on **Understanding APIs**.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,

• Define what an **API** is.
• Explain the role of an **API** in **AI** applications.
• Identify how **API** keys secure access.
• Describe the flow of requests and responses via **APIs**.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Pre-requisites
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you should be familiar with **Python** basics.
These basics are covered in Episode 1: **Python** basics for **API**.

slides.title: What is an API? The Digital Connector
slides.narration:
Have you ever wondered how different software applications talk to each other?
An **API**, or Application Programming Interface, is that digital connector.
It allows various software applications to communicate seamlessly.
Think of an **API** like a waiter in a restaurant.
You give your order, or **request**, to the waiter.
The waiter takes your order to the kitchen, which is like the **AI** model.
Then, the waiter brings back your meal, or the **response**.
That's how an **API** works to connect different parts.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing API as a waiter connecting a customer (application) to a kitchen (AI model)

slides.title: Sending Prompts through APIs
slides.narration:
Now, how do we tell an **AI** model what we want it to do?
In **AI** applications, we send **prompts** through an **API**.
These **prompts** are specific instructions or data.
The **AI** model then processes these **prompts**.
It generates the desired output based on your instructions.
So, an **API** is the bridge for your **prompts** to reach the **AI**.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a prompt being sent through an API to an AI model

slides.title: API Keys: Your Access Pass
slides.narration:
But how do **APIs** ensure that only authorized users or applications can access them?
This is where **API** keys come in.
**API** keys are unique identifiers.
They are used for authentication and access control.
They ensure that only authorized applications can interact with the **API**.
This protects both the service and your valuable user data.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a key unlocking access to an API

slides.title: How Applications Use APIs
slides.narration:
Let's put it all together and see how applications use **APIs**.
First, your application sends a **request** to an **API**.
The **API** then relays this **request** to an **AI** model for processing.
Once the **AI** model generates a **response**, the **API** takes it.
It then delivers the **response** back to your application.
This completes the entire communication cycle smoothly.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing the flow from application sending a request, through API, to AI model, and back with a response

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined **APIs** as digital connectors.
We explored how **prompts** are sent through them.
We understood the role of **API** keys for security.
Finally, we traced the request-response flow in **AI** applications.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now as an assignment,
Explore the documentation of a public **API**, like a weather **API**.
Identify its key endpoints and required authentication methods.
Compare the results.
